Couple Ministry
KUH-puhl MIN-uh-stree
noun
The joint service of a husband and wife in the work of the gospel, as Aquila and Priscilla; ministry shared within the marriage bond.

Biblical Definition

Couple ministry is the joint service of a husband and wife in the work of the gospel—the two who are one flesh laboring together for Christ, as heirs together of the grace of life. The chief biblical example is Aquila and Priscilla, the tentmaking couple who were Paul’s helpers in Christ Jesus, who hosted a church in their house, and who together took the eloquent Apollos and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly. Their partnership shows the strength of a believing marriage poured out in service: hospitality, instruction, the risking of their own necks for Paul, the building up of the church—done together. Scripture teaches that the husband and wife are heirs together of the grace of life, and that two are better than one, a threefold cord not quickly broken. The dictionary commends such joint ministry while keeping it within the biblical order it everywhere honors: the husband and wife serve as complementary partners, the wife a true fellow-laborer, yet the order of headship is not erased, and the public office of teaching and ruling in the gathered church remains with qualified men—Priscilla instructed Apollos privately, alongside her husband, not as an ordained teacher over the assembly. The dictionary reads couple ministry as the fruitful labor of a believing husband and wife together for the gospel—a threefold cord of the two and the Lord—exercised in hospitality, discipleship, and service, within the creational order and to the building up of Christ’s church.

Webster 1828 Definition

Key Scripture

Act 18:26 — "And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly."

Rom 16:3 — "Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus:"

1Pe 3:7 — "Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered."

Ecc 4:12 — "And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken."

Modern Corruption

Couple ministry is misused to erase the order of headship and to install women in the office of teaching and ruling the church; rightly kept, it is fruitful partnership within the creational order.

expand to see more

The misuse to name is the pressing of couple ministry, and of Priscilla’s example, into an argument against the biblical order—as though her instructing of Apollos overturned the apostolic word that a woman is not to teach or usurp authority over the man in the church, and as though joint ministry meant the erasing of headship and the installing of wives in the office of elder. But Priscilla and Aquila instructed Apollos privately, together, in their home—not in the public assembly, and not as an ordained teacher ruling the congregation. The complementarian order the dictionary everywhere honors is not abolished by a believing wife’s true and valuable labor; the two truths stand together.

The principle to recover is fruitful partnership within the creational order. The believing husband and wife are heirs together of the grace of life, a threefold cord with the Lord not quickly broken, and their joint labor in hospitality, discipleship, and service is a great strength to the church, as Aquila and Priscilla’s was to Paul. The wife is a true fellow-laborer, honored and valued, her gifts employed; yet the husband’s headship is not erased, and the public office of teaching and ruling the gathered church remains with qualified men. Couple ministry honors both the partnership and the order, and is the more fruitful for keeping them together.
